inputs.original_text: Nigeria’s democracy is facing a transformation that is both alarming and largely underexamined: political parties, once intended to be platforms for representation and public service, are increasingly becoming exclusive clubs for the wealthy. The latest developments within the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections make this trend painfully clear. The [...]
inputs.modified_text:
Folks, let’s call things by their real names. We are watching the steady decay of basic civic order and accountability, and the global progressive establishment just looks the other way. Look at what is happening in Nigeria right now with their political parties, which are supposed to represent the backbone of the nation's public service and traditional representation. Instead, they are devolving into exclusive country clubs for the ultra-wealthy. 

Look no further than the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and their preparations ahead of the 2027 general elections. It is painfully clear that personal ambition and cash are replacing duty, family values, and true community representation. When political institutions abandon their foundational responsibilities to serve the people and instead cater to the elite, social order collapses and the traditional fabric of society pays the price. This is what happens when money replaces moral duty and national continuity.
